Subject: GatewayCorp GRC - penetration assessment artifact required

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick onboarding last week. As part of our SIG/CAIQ review and SOC 2 refresh, our GRC team requires a copy of your most recent penetration assessment for the product endpoints that GatewayCorp integrates with (public API, auth service, and embedding ingestion pipeline). Our portal flags the absence of this artifact and has set a 2026-11-10 deadline to avoid escalation.

Requested items (from the portal):
- Final penetration assessment report (PDF).
- Scope section listing in-scope assets and test dates.
- A remediation status matrix (or a link to a tracker) showing fixes and verification.

We understand some PoCs and internal IP addresses may need redaction — please indicate what you can provide and whether redacted delivery is acceptable. If you have a short FAQ about redaction policy we can accept, that helps expedite review.

Portal link to upload: https://grc.gatewaycorp.com/records/RECORD-9281 (email grc-portal@gatewaycorp.com if you hit a permissions issue).

Appreciate a quick note on scope and an ETA.

—Alex Mercer
Head of Vendor Risk, GatewayCorp
security@gatewaycorp.com

Subject: Re: GatewayCorp GRC - penetration assessment artifact required

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the portal link. We can provide a redacted copy of the final penetration assessment; before we upload I have a couple quick clarifying questions so we deliver exactly what your reviewers expect:

1) Redaction guidance: we typically redact PoC exploit code, attacker IPs, and internal contact emails. Is that acceptable to your GRC team?
2) Retest evidence: do you need proof of remediation verification (e.g., retest report or vulnerability verification notes), or is a remediation snapshot + planned retest date sufficient?
3) Scope granularity: should the scope list include hostnames/IP ranges and cloud account IDs, or is a high-level list (API endpoints, auth service, ingestion) acceptable?

Plan from our side: we will prepare a redacted PDF and an accompanying remediation snapshot (spreadsheet) and aim to upload by 2026-11-04. If Gateway needs unredacted evidence for a privileged review, we can discuss an accredited NDA/secure view workflow.

Assigning internally: Laura — can you confirm the latest pen-test file and whether the vendor redacted PoCs already? Neha — can you prepare the remediation tracker export (status + verification notes)?

Thanks,

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: GatewayCorp GRC - penetration assessment artifact required

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick reply and proposed timeline. The GRC review can accept redactions with the following constraints:
- Redact PoC code and any customer-identifying data.
- Do NOT redact scope definitions (hostnames, CIDR ranges) — we need to confirm what was tested. Cloud account IDs may be obfuscated (e.g., ACCOUNT-XXXX) but indicate which environment (prod/staging).
- Include test dates, tester/vendor name, and high-level methodology (black-box/white-box).
- For each finding, include severity, remediation status (open/fixed), and a verification column (retest date or verification evidence).

Regarding retest evidence: a re-test report is ideal for critical/high findings. For medium/low, a remediation snapshot with verification notes is acceptable. If fixes were validated internally, include who validated and when.

If you cannot meet the 11/10 deadline for full unredacted delivery, please upload the redacted report and remediation snapshot to the portal now and then send a secure invitation for a privileged review of unredacted artifacts (we will provide access instructions).

Portal note: when you upload, use the "Vendor: Final Assessment" category so it routes to the right reviewer.

Best,

GatewayCorp Vendor Risk (on behalf of Alex)
security@gatewaycorp.com
